message.content:
Hawaii’s climate is tropical, so it stays warm year‑round, but there are still seasonal variations that affect both weather and crowd levels:

| Season | Typical Weather | Crowds & Prices |
|--------|-----------------|-----------------|
| **Peak season** (Dec–Jan, Jul–Aug) | Warmest days (~80 °F/27 °C), higher humidity, occasional showers | Highest visitor numbers, higher accommodation rates |
| **Shoulder seasons** (Apr–Jun, Sep–Nov) | Pleasant temperatures (70–80 °F / 21–27 °C), lower humidity, less rain | Fewer tourists, better deals on flights/hotels |
| **Low season** (Feb–Mar, Dec–Jan) | Slightly cooler mornings/evenings (~65–75 °F / 18–24 °C), more rain | Lower prices, but some resorts may have reduced services |

### Bottom line
If you’re looking for the most comfortable conditions with fewer crowds and better value, the **shoulder periods—late spring (April–June) and early fall (September–November)—are generally considered the “best” times to visit**. During these months you’ll enjoy sunny skies, clear waters, and a relaxed atmosphere while still benefiting from relatively mild temperatures.
